* साधक-संजीवनी *
६७
हैं। इसलिये श्लोकके उत्तरार्धमें भगवान् सबसे पहले | है, यह इस लोकमें भी कीर्ति (यश) देनेवाली नहीं है,
उपर्युक्त पद देकर कहते हैं कि तुम्हारेमें जो कायरता आयी प्रत्युत अपकीर्ति (अपयश ) देनेवाली है । अत: तुम्हारेमें
है, उस कायरताको श्रेष्ठ पुरुष स्वीकार नहीं करते। कारण कायरताका आना सर्वथा ही अनुचित है ।
कि तुम्हारी इस कायरतामें अपने कल्याणकी बात बिलकुल
नहीं है। कल्याण चाहनेवाले श्रेष्ठ मनुष्य प्रवृत्ति और
निवृत्ति दोनोंमें अपने कल्याणका ही उद्देश्य रखते हैं।
उनमें अपने कर्तव्यके प्रति कायरता उत्पन्न नहीं होती ।
परिस्थितिके अनुसार उनको जो कर्तव्य प्राप्त हो जाता है,
उसको वे कल्याणप्राप्तिके उद्देश्यसे उत्साह और तत्परतापूर्वक
सांगोपांग करते हैं। वे तुम्हारे - जैसे कायर होकर युद्धसे या
अन्य किसी कर्तव्य-कर्मसे उपरत नहीं होते । अतः युद्ध -
रूपसे प्राप्त कर्तव्य-कर्मसे उपरत होना तुम्हारे लिये
कल्याणकारक नहीं है।
|
'अस्वर्ग्यम्' – कल्याणकी बात सामने न रखकर
अगर सांसारिक दृष्टिसे भी देखा जाय, तो संसारमें
स्वर्गलोक ऊँचा है। परन्तु तुम्हारी यह कायरता स्वर्गको
देनेवाली भी नहीं है अर्थात् कायरतापूर्वक युद्धसे निवृत्त
होनेका फल स्वर्गकी प्राप्ति भी नहीं हो सकता ।
भगवान्ने यहाँ ‘अनार्यजुष्टम्' 'अस्वर्ग्यम्' और
'अकीर्तिकरम् ' - ऐसा क्रम देकर तीन प्रकारके मनुष्य
बताये हैं - (१) जो विचारशील मनुष्य होते हैं, वे केवल
अपना कल्याण ही चाहते हैं । उनका ध्येय, उद्देश्य केवल
कल्याणका ही होता है। (२) जो पुण्यात्मा मनुष्य होते हैं,
वे शुभ - कर्मोंके द्वारा स्वर्गकी प्राप्ति चाहते हैं । वे स्वर्गको
ही श्रेष्ठ मानकर उसकी प्राप्तिका ही उद्देश्य रखते हैं
(३) जो साधारण मनुष्य होते हैं, वे संसारको ही आदर
देते हैं । इसलिये वे संसारमें अपनी कीर्ति चाहते हैं और
उस कीर्तिको ही अपना ध्येय मानते हैं ।

english:
Shloka 3
* Sādhaka-Sanjīvanī *
67

Therefore, in the latter part of the shloka, the Lord first says that the cowardice that has arisen in you is not only not going to give you fame (yash) in this world, but on the contrary, it will give you infamy (apayash). Hence, the noble persons do not accept the cowardice that is in you, because the advent of cowardice is entirely inappropriate. 

The reason is that in your cowardice, there is not even a bit of consideration for your own welfare. Desirous of welfare, noble men always keep their welfare in mind, whether they are engaged in action (pravritti) or withdrawn from action (nivritti). In them, cowardice is not born with regard to their duty. According to the circumstances, whatever duty they get, they perform it with enthusiasm and promptness, with the aim of achieving their welfare. They do not become cowardly like you and refrain from war or any other duty. Therefore, to refrain from the duty that has come to you in the form of war is not beneficial for you.

'Asvargyam' – If we do not consider the aspect of welfare and look at it from a worldly point of view, then in the world, Svarga (heaven) is considered superior. However, your cowardice will not even lead to Svarga, meaning that the result of retreating from war out of cowardice cannot be the attainment of Svarga.

The Lord has mentioned three types of men here by using the words 'anāryajuṣṭam', 'asvargyam', and 'akīrtikaram' – 
1. Those who are thoughtful and consider only their welfare as their goal.
2. The pious ones who, through good deeds, aim for the attainment of Svarga, considering it superior.
3. Ordinary people who respect the world and thus desire fame in the world, making it their goal.

By mentioning these three terms, the Lord cautions Arjuna that his decision not to fight is not conducive to the goals of thoughtful and pious men, namely, welfare and the attainment of Svarga, nor does it lead to the goal of ordinary men, which is fame.

'Akīrtikaram' – Even if one does not have the goal of attaining Svarga, a respectable person performs actions that bring fame in the world. However, your cowardice, which leads to retreating from war or other duties, will not bring you fame. On the contrary, due to delusion, your decision not to fight is so base that it will lead to your downfall, take you to hell, and bring you infamy.

#### Connection
After the onset of cowardice, what should be done now? To dispel this inquiry, the Lord says:

klayvam mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitattvayyupapadyate |
kṣudram hṛdayadaurbalyam tyaktvottīṣṭha parantapa || 3 ||

- **klayvam** = this weakness, this impotence
- **mā sma gamaḥ** = do not yield to
- **pārtha** = O son of Pritha (Arjuna)
- **naitat** = this
- **tvayi** = in you
- **upapadyate** = is not fitting
- **kṣudram** = this base, this trivial
- **hṛdayadaurbalyam** = heart's weakness
- **tyaktvā** = having abandoned
- **uttīṣṭha** = arise
- **parantapa** = O scorcher of enemies (Arjuna)

#### Explanation
'Pārtha'* – By reminding Arjuna of his mother Pritha (Kunti), the Lord addresses him, evoking the memory of his lineage. 'Pārtha' is another name for Arjuna, being the son of Pritha (Kunti). The 'Pārtha' address is an indicator of the Lord's affection and closeness to Arjuna. In the Gita, the Lord has used the 'Pārtha' address thirty-eight times, more than any other address for Arjuna. The next most frequent address used for Arjuna is 'Kaunteya', which appears twenty-four times.

Whenever the Lord wants to convey something special to Arjuna, or offer him assurance, or when His affection for Arjuna overflows, He addresses him as 'Pārtha'. This address serves as a reminder that Arjuna is not only the son of His aunt (Pritha – Kunti) but also His beloved devotee and friend. Thus, the Lord shares special, confidential matters with Arjuna and whatever He says is true and solely for Arjuna's benefit.
